requirement:
# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283

#### Bug description

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a **closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly**.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with **no generated resolver at all**. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime. In our case three assemblies of a large app had been shipping without a resolver across two releases before we noticed.

#### Repro steps

Two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`. Both projects are in the attached `mp-repro.zip`.

#### Expected behavior

A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.
#### Actual behavior

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`.

- Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8
- Runtime: .NET 10 (SDK 10.0.204), Windows 11

#### Additional context

**What triggers it.** `Item` is declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`:

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the crash disappear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.
**Stack trace.**

```
System.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol)
   at TypeCollector.CollectGeneric(INamedTypeSymbol type, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 661
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 371
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 1062
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 386
   at TypeCollector.Collect() in TypeCollector.cs:line 300
   at MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.AnalyzeSymbol(SymbolAnalysisContext, ReferenceSymbols, AnalyzerOptions) in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs:line 431
```

`CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly:

```csharp
else
{
    // NOTE: ... closed generic types such as `Foo<string>` are not registered as a formatter.
    this.GetObjectInfo(type, callerSymbol);
```

so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` the way the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers already do, and that collection is empty for a metadata symbol. I did not narrow down which of the three fires.

**Getting the stack trace.** Console output truncates the exception to its message; `-p:ErrorLog=out.sarif` preserves the full description, including the stack trace and an `ISymbol:` context line naming the offending type:

```
dotnet build -p:ErrorLog=out.sarif
```

**Workaround.** Putting `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` (line 356) before `GetObjectInfo` is reached, at the cost of hand-writing the formatter.

**Possibly related:** #2092 reports CS8785 from the v3 generator, but with a different inner exception and no repro.

story.summary: Stops the generator and analyzer from crashing when a [MessagePackObject] member's type is a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly. Two places that read `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` now tolerate a missing source declaration (lines 985, 1077). The analyzer's report callback is also wrapped (line 239) so that any diagnostic without a source location inside the current compilation is silently dropped. Three new tests compile a library to a metadata-only image and check that the consumer builds with no diagnostics and gets a resolver. README and MsgPack004 docs are extended.
story.why: REQ-2283: the IndexOutOfRangeException made the generator contribute nothing, so the consuming assembly shipped with no generated resolver and failed under trimming/NativeAOT.
touches_beyond_requirement: The filter at line 239/1444-1450 applies to every diagnostic the TypeCollector reports, not just ones about metadata symbols. Any diagnostic with Location.None or a null location is now dropped, including ones about source types.
New README section and MsgPack004.md section describe a policy for user-visible diagnostics: they are 'reported by the assembly that defines it'.
Test ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember enshrines that a missing-key member on a referenced type produces no diagnostic in the consumer.
story.confidence_overview: High that the reported repro (record struct Item<T> from metadata) no longer crashes: test 2 mirrors the issue exactly and also checks that the resolver hint name is produced. Medium that all crash sites are covered. The issue names three `[0]` indexing sites and the diff visibly changes two. Low-to-medium on the side effects of the blanket diagnostic filter, which no test exercises for source types.

claims.text: The tests reproduce the issue using a real metadata-only reference, not a same-compilation project reference. Test 2 matches the issue's Item<T>/Cmd repro verbatim. Each test fails on any analyzer or generator diagnostic and asserts that the expected resolver hint name is generated.
claims.requirement_quote: A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

breaker.reason: While CompileToMetadataReferenceAsync creates a real PE image MetadataReference (GenericsFormatterTests.cs line 673) and VerifyCS.Test fails on diagnostics and checks the resolver hint name (lines 638-658), Test 2 does not match the issue's Item<T>/Cmd repro verbatim: ClosedGenericRecordStruct_FromMetadataReference adds an explicit [GeneratedMessagePackResolver] partial class AppResolver { } on lines 575-576 and asserts App.AppResolver.g.cs on line 579, whereas the issue's app repro has no [GeneratedMessagePackResolver] declaration and relies on implicit default GeneratedMessagePackResolver generation (which none of the three new tests exercise). In addition, CompileToMetadataReferenceAsync (lines 661-674) compiles defineSource without running MessagePackGenerator on Lib, unlike dotnet build on the repro's lib project.

claims.text: The BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic no longer indexes DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]. It uses a helper that returns null when the property has no source declaration.
claims.requirement_quote: Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly

breaker.reason: Checked TypeCollector.cs line 985 and line 1434: BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull now calls GetPropertyIdentifierLocation(item) instead of indexing DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0], and GetPropertyIdentifierLocation uses DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault() so it returns null when a property has no source declaration.

claims.text: The MemberNeedsKey diagnostic, which is built eagerly even when reportDiagnostic is null (so it also crashed the generator), now uses FirstOrDefault() and produces a null location instead of throwing.

breaker.reason: Checked TypeCollector.cs lines 1075-1081: Diagnostic.Create for MemberNeedsKey is evaluated eagerly on lines 1075-1077 before checking accessibility or invoking this.reportDiagnostic?.Invoke on line 1080, so it ran even when reportDiagnostic was null in the generator. Line 1077 now uses DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation(), yielding null instead of throwing IndexOutOfRangeException, and ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember (GenericsFormatterTests.cs lines 590-626) exercises both the analyzer and generator paths.

claims.text: Diagnostics whose location is not a source location within the current compilation are dropped before reaching the analyzer's report callback.
claims.requirement_quote: so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax

breaker.reason: Checked TypeCollector.cs lines 239 and 1444-1450: this.reportDiagnostic wraps reportAnalyzerDiagnostic in ReportIfLocatedInCompilation, which only forwards diagnostics when diagnostic.Location.IsInSource is true and this.compilation.ContainsSyntaxTree(diagnostic.Location.SourceTree) is true, dropping Location.None, metadata locations, and syntax trees from other compilations. Verified that ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember exercises dropping the Location.None MemberNeedsKey diagnostic.

claims.text: The content of the generated formatter for the referenced generic struct is not verified. SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck is set, and only the hint name is checked.

breaker.reason: Checked GenericsFormatterTests.cs line 641 and lines 657-658: TestBehaviors.SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck skips snapshot verification of the generated formatter and resolver source text, and the CSharpGeneratorDriver check only asserts that expectedResolverHintName is present in GeneratedSources.

claims.text: Scope: no public API or analyzer rule descriptors are added. However, the observable set of diagnostics changes: located-outside-compilation and location-less diagnostics are suppressed, and docs are added describing this.

breaker.reason: Checked TypeCollector.cs lines 1444-1450, README.md lines 1639-1642, and doc/analyzers/MsgPack004.md lines 49-52: no public API or analyzer rule descriptors are added, ReportIfLocatedInCompilation suppresses both outside-compilation and location-less diagnostics, and documentation is added describing referenced-assembly diagnostic behavior.

refusals.what: Analyzer diagnostics (e.g. MsgPack004 MemberNeedsKey) are no longer reported for referenced-assembly types or for any location-less diagnostic.
refusals.why: This changes user-visible analyzer behavior and documents a new policy. A maintainer should decide whether suppression, rather than reporting at the consumer's member location, is the intended contract.

refusals.what: The fix includes a global diagnostic filter plus README/MsgPack004 documentation, beyond the null-safe indexing the requirement points to.
refusals.why: These are changes beyond the requirement whose side effects on source-type diagnostics are untested.

findings.description: Claim C4 disputed: While CompileToMetadataReferenceAsync creates a real PE image MetadataReference (GenericsFormatterTests.cs line 673) and VerifyCS.Test fails on diagnostics and checks the resolver hint name (lines 638-658), Test 2 does not match the issue's Item<T>/Cmd repro verbatim: ClosedGenericRecordStruct_FromMetadataReference adds an explicit [GeneratedMessagePackResolver] partial class AppResolver { } on lines 575-576 and asserts App.AppResolver.g.cs on line 579, whereas the issue's app repro has no [GeneratedMessagePackResolver] declaration and relies on implicit default GeneratedMessagePackResolver generation (which none of the three new tests exercise). In addition, CompileToMetadataReferenceAsync (lines 661-674) compiles defineSource without running MessagePackGenerator on Lib, unlike dotnet build on the repro's lib project.

The issue lists three `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites (reported at lines 735, 1009, 1101). The diff visibly changes only two (around 985 and 1077). If a third site remains near the earlier location, it can still throw in the analyzer, where reportDiagnostic is non-null. This would happen for metadata types that hit that path, which the three new tests may not exercise. Worth grepping for remaining `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]`.

The filter drops every diagnostic whose Location is not in source, including Location.None. Any existing diagnostic about a source type that is created with a null location gets silently swallowed instead of reported. Examples are GetIdentifierLocation/GetParameterListLocation returning null, or AOTDerivedKeyAttribute from an attribute in another tree. This is a broader behavior change than the crash fix, and no test covers it.

The docs claim member diagnostics for referenced types 'are reported by the assembly that defines it'. That only holds if the defining assembly was built with the MessagePack analyzer. For a third-party NuGet package built without it, problems such as an unkeyed public member are now reported nowhere, and the consumer silently generates a formatter for that type.

The UnkeyedMember test asserts that a missing-key member on a referenced type produces no diagnostic and still generates a resolver. It does not check what the generated formatter does with the unkeyed member. This locks in the suppression policy without showing the serialized result is sensible.

GetPropertyIdentifierLocation casts property.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax() as PropertyDeclarationSyntax. For a positional record or record struct property declared in source in the current compilation (e.g., [MessagePackObject] public record Rec([property: Key((string)null!)] string Key);), Roslyn's declaring syntax is ParameterSyntax rather than PropertyDeclarationSyntax, so GetPropertyIdentifierLocation returns null. Combined with ReportIfLocatedInCompilation (line 1446) dropping Location.None diagnostics, BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull (line 985) is silently suppressed for positional record properties in the current compilation.

ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops all diagnostics with !diagnostic.Location.IsInSource (including Location.None) instead of checking whether the analyzed symbol belongs to the current compilation. Existing helpers in TypeCollector such as GetParameterListLocation(IMethodSymbol? method) at line 1454 return null (producing Location.None) when method is null or an implicitly declared constructor with empty DeclaringSyntaxReferences on a source type in the current compilation; previously Roslyn allowed reporting those Location.None diagnostics, whereas now they are silently swallowed.

README.md line 1642 and doc/analyzers/MsgPack004.md line 52 state that member diagnostics for types from a referenced assembly are reported by the defining assembly, but a defining assembly that only references MessagePack.Annotations (without MessagePack.SourceGenerator, as in CompileToMetadataReferenceAsync at GenericsFormatterTests.cs line 664) runs no analyzers, and ReportIfLocatedInCompilation now drops those diagnostics in the consuming project too, leaving unkeyed public members on referenced generic types silently omitted from generated formatters with no warning in either project.

out_of_scope.description: New user-facing section on generic types from referenced assemblies and diagnostic ownership. Not required to fix the crash.
New section stating that the analyzer only reports on members declared in the current project.
Blanket ReportIfLocatedInCompilation wrapper applied to all reported diagnostics. It goes beyond making the two indexing sites null-safe.
